assumptions.assumption: Lidar‑based tracking yields accurate mover positions/velocities within ~0.5 m
assumptions.why: Collision occurred despite mover being detected at 0.89 m; repeated stop‑turns indicate tracking lag or missed updates

assumptions.assumption: Time‑augmented A* on a 0.2 m grid can always find a feasible detour around a mover within the 3 s horizon
assumptions.why: Multiple runs stalled with no progress, suggesting _replan_route often returned None

assumptions.assumption: A planning horizon of 3 s is sufficient to predict mover motion for safe avoidance
assumptions.why: Movers are small boxes moving ≤2 m/s; 3 s horizon covers most trajectories, but A* still fails to use the prediction

assumptions.assumption: After a pause the robot can safely resume waypoint following without additional checks
assumptions.why: Robot resumed after pause and collided; also spent long time rotating without progress

assumptions.assumption: Safe distance of 3.0 m triggers replanning early enough to avoid collision
assumptions.why: Replan was triggered (first_not_on_map at 0.89 m), but A* could not produce a path

assumptions.assumption: Fallback mechanisms (escape, detour, side_detour) will be invoked when A* fails
assumptions.why: Robot remained in stop‑turn loops; fallback functions never produced a viable command

candidates.idea: Make the VO planner the primary local avoidance method when a mover is within _SAFE_DIST, using it every control step and falling back to A* only if VO cannot find any safe velocity for >1 s
candidates.for: VO directly handles moving obstacles without relying on a static grid that often fails, reducing stalls and collisions
candidates.risk: VO may produce oscillatory commands in cluttered static scenes or may be too conservative, causing slower progress

candidates.idea: Replace the A* replanner with a continuous DWA that evaluates candidate (v,w) against both static map and unmapped points each step, selecting the safest velocity; keep A* only for long‑term waypoint updates
candidates.for: DWA provides reactive, velocity‑level avoidance and can operate even when the grid planner fails
candidates.risk: Higher computational load and possible over‑conservatism leading to longer pauses

candidates.idea: Introduce a predictive wait strategy: when a mover is detected within _SAFE_DIST, estimate its crossing time and pause only until the mover is expected to have cleared, with a maximum wait of 4 s; if the wait expires, switch to VO avoidance
candidates.for: Avoids endless stop‑turn cycles by limiting pause duration and providing a fallback
candidates.risk: Incorrect crossing‑time estimation could cause premature motion and collision

diagnosis_out.chosen: Use the VO planner as the primary avoidance method (candidate 1) because it directly reasons about moving obstacles and avoids the brittle A* grid failures that caused stalls and collisions.
diagnosis_out.target: controller (the decision block that selects replanning vs pause vs speed)
diagnosis_out.direction: 1. In controller(), after _perceive() compute M and check _min_gap(pose, M). 2. If the gap ≤ _SAFE_DIST, call _vo_planner(st, pose, wp, M) with strict=False. 3. If _vo_planner returns (v,w), set vc=v and w_nom=w, skip the A* replanning block entirely. 4. If VO returns None for more than 1.0 s, fall back to the existing A* replanner as a long‑term path generator. 5. When VO provides a command, still pass (vc,w) through _guard() for final safety checks. 6. Reset st["plan_until"] and st["pause_until"] appropriately when switching between VO and A* to avoid stale timers.
